title: Human-in-the-Loop Uncertainty Analysis in Self-Adaptive Robots Using LLMs
summary: Self-adaptive robots operate in dynamic, unpredictable environments where unaddressed uncertainties can lead to safety violations and operational failures. However, systematically identifying and analyzing these uncertainties, including their sources, impacts, and mitigation strategies, remains a significant challenge given the inherent complexity of real-world environments, dynamic robotic behavior, and the rapid evolution of robotic technologies. To address this, we introduce RoboULM, a human-in-the-loop methodology and tool that supports practitioners in systematically exploring uncertainties at the design stage using large language models (LLMs). Moreover, we present an uncertainty taxonomy that provides a detailed catalog of uncertainties in self-adaptive robots. We evaluated RoboULM with 16 practitioners from four industrial use cases. The results show that RoboULM was perceived as both useful and easy to understand, with the participants particularly valuing structured prompting and iterative refinement support. These findings demonstrate the potential of RoboULM as a viable solution for systematic uncertainty analysis in complex robots.

AI.tldr: RoboULM is a human-in-the-loop methodology using LLMs to help practitioners systematically identify and analyze uncertainties in self-adaptive robots at design time, supported by an uncertainty taxonomy. Evaluated with 16 practitioners across four industrial use cases, it was perceived as useful and easy to understand.
AI.motivation: Self-adaptive robots face dynamic, unpredictable environments where unaddressed uncertainties cause safety violations and failures, yet systematic identification and analysis of uncertainties remains challenging due to environmental complexity, dynamic behavior, and rapid tech evolution.
AI.method: RoboULM is a human-in-the-loop methodology and tool leveraging large language models (LLMs) with structured prompting and iterative refinement support, combined with an uncertainty taxonomy for cataloging uncertainties in self-adaptive robots.
AI.result: Evaluation with 16 practitioners from four industrial use cases showed RoboULM was perceived as useful and easy to understand; participants particularly valued structured prompting and iterative refinement support.
AI.conclusion: RoboULM demonstrates potential as a viable solution for systematic uncertainty analysis in complex self-adaptive robots.

title: Refining Compositional Diffusion for Reliable Long-Horizon Planning
summary: Compositional diffusion planning generates long-horizon trajectories by stitching together overlapping short-horizon segments through score composition. However, when local plan distributions are multimodal, existing compositional methods suffer from mode-averaging, where averaging incompatible local modes leads to plans that are neither locally feasible nor globally coherent. We propose Refining Compositional Diffusion (RCD), a training-free guidance method that steers compositional sampling toward high-density, globally coherent plans. RCD leverages the self-reconstruction error of a pretrained diffusion model as a proxy for the log-density of composed plans, combined with an overlap consistency term that enforces consistency at segment boundaries. We show that the combined guidance concentrates sampling on high-density plans that mitigate mode-averaging. Experiments on challenging long-horizon tasks from OGBench, including locomotion, object manipulation, and pixel-based observations, demonstrate that RCD consistently outperforms existing methods.

AI.tldr: RCD is a training-free guidance method that refines compositional diffusion planning by using self-reconstruction error and overlap consistency to avoid mode-averaging, enabling better long-horizon trajectory generation across diverse tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing compositional diffusion planning suffers from mode-averaging when local plan distributions are multimodal, leading to plans that are neither locally feasible nor globally coherent.
AI.method: RCD is a training-free guidance method that uses the self-reconstruction error of a pretrained diffusion model as a proxy for log-density of composed plans, combined with an overlap consistency term that enforces consistency at segment boundaries, to steer compositional sampling toward high-density, globally coherent plans.
AI.result: RCD consistently outperforms existing methods on challenging long-horizon tasks from OGBench, including locomotion, object manipulation, and pixel-based observations.
AI.conclusion: The combined guidance of self-reconstruction error and overlap consistency concentrates sampling on high-density plans that mitigate mode-averaging, producing globally coherent long-horizon trajectories.

title: Benchmarking Local Language Models for Social Robots using Edge Devices
comment: Accepted for 22nd IEEE International Conference on Advanced Robotics and its Social Impact (June 2026) in Vienna, Austria
summary:
Social-educational robots designed for socially interactive pedagogical support, such as the Robot Study Companion (RSC), rely on responsive, privacy-preserving interaction despite severely limited compute. However, there is a gap in systematic benchmarking of language models for edge computing in pedagogical applications. This paper benchmarks 25 open-source language models for local deployment on edge hardware. We evaluate each model across three dimensions: inference efficiency (tokens per second, energy consumption), general knowledge (a six-category MMLU subset), and teaching effectiveness (LLM-rated pedagogical quality), validated against five independent human raters using the Raspberry Pi(RPi)4 as the primary platform, with additional comparisons on the RPi5 and a laptop GPU.
  Results reveal pronounced trade-offs: throughput and energy efficiency vary by over an order of magnitude across models, MMLU accuracy ranges from near-random to 57.2%, and teaching effectiveness does not correlate monotonically with either metric. Among the evaluated models, Granite4 Tiny Hybrid (7B) achieves a strong overall balance, reaching 2.5 tokens per second, 0.90 tokens per joule, and 54.6% MMLU accuracy; high MMLU accuracy does not appear necessary for strong teaching scores. Human validation on four representative models preserved the automated rank ordering (Pearson r = 0.967, n = 4). Based on these findings, we propose a three-tier local inference architecture for the RSC that balances responsiveness and accuracy on resource-constrained hardware.

AI.tldr: This paper benchmarks 25 open-source language models for edge deployment on pedagogical robots, evaluating inference efficiency, general knowledge (MMLU), and teaching effectiveness. Results show significant trade-offs; Granite4 Tiny Hybrid (7B) achieves the best balance. Human validation confirms automated rankings (r=0.967). A three-tier local inference architecture is proposed for the Robot Study Companion.
AI.motivation: Social-educational robots like the Robot Study Companion (RSC) need privacy-preserving, responsive interaction on severely limited compute, but there is a lack of systematic benchmarking of language models for edge computing in pedagogical applications.
AI.method: 25 open-source language models were benchmarked on edge hardware (Raspberry Pi 4/5, laptop GPU) across three dimensions: inference efficiency (tokens/s, energy consumption), general knowledge (six-category MMLU subset), and teaching effectiveness (LLM-rated pedagogical quality validated against five human raters).
AI.result: Throughput and energy efficiency vary by over an order of magnitude; MMLU accuracy ranges from near-random to 57.2%; teaching effectiveness does not correlate monotonically with either metric. Granite4 Tiny Hybrid (7B) achieves the best balance (2.5 tokens/s, 0.90 tokens/joule, 54.6% MMLU). Human validation preserved automated rank ordering (Pearson r=0.967, n=4).
AI.conclusion: High MMLU accuracy is not necessary for strong teaching scores. A three-tier local inference architecture is proposed for the RSC to balance responsiveness and accuracy on resource-constrained hardware.

title: Robust Path Tracking for Vehicles via Continuous-Time Residual Learning: An ICODE-MPPI Approach
summary: Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control is a powerful sampling-based strategy for nonlinear autonomous systems. However, its performance is often bottlenecked by the fidelity of nominal dynamics. We propose ICODE-MPPI, a robust framework that leverages Input Concomitant Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (ICODEs) to learn and compensate for unmodeled residual dynamics. Unlike discrete-time learners, ICODEs maintain physical consistency and temporal continuity during the MPPI prediction horizon. High-fidelity simulations on complex trajectories demonstrate that ICODE-MPPI achieves up to a 69\% reduction in cross-tracking error under persistent disturbances compared to standard MPPI control. Furthermore, our analysis confirms that ICODE-MPPI significantly suppresses control chattering, yielding smoother steering commands and superior robust performance.

AI.tldr: ICODE-MPPI integrates Input Concomitant Neural ODEs into MPPI control to learn and compensate for unmodeled dynamics, achieving up to 69% reduction in cross-tracking error and smoother control under disturbances.
AI.motivation: Standard MPPI control performance is limited by the fidelity of nominal dynamics, suffering from unmodeled residual dynamics that degrade tracking accuracy and control smoothness.
AI.method: The method replaces discrete-time learners with Input Concomitant Neural ODEs (ICODEs) to model residual dynamics, maintaining physical consistency and temporal continuity throughout the MPPI prediction horizon.
AI.result: ICODE-MPPI achieves up to 69% reduction in cross-tracking error under persistent disturbances and significantly suppresses control chattering compared to standard MPPI.
AI.conclusion: ICODE-MPPI provides a robust, physically consistent framework for compensating unmodeled dynamics in sampling-based nonlinear control, yielding smoother and more accurate trajectory tracking.

title: CreativityBench: Evaluating Agent Creative Reasoning via Affordance-Based Tool Repurposing
summary: Recent advances in large language models have led to strong performance on reasoning and environment-interaction tasks, yet their ability for creative problem-solving remains underexplored. We study this capability through the lens of creative tool use, where a model repurposes available objects by reasoning about their affordances and attributes rather than relying on canonical usage. As a first step, we introduce CreativityBench, a benchmark for evaluating affordance-based creativity in LLMs. To this end, we build a large-scale affordance knowledge base (KB) with 4K entities and 150K+ affordance annotations, explicitly linking objects, parts, attributes, and actionable uses. Building on this KB, we generate 14K grounded tasks that require identifying non-obvious yet physically plausible solutions under constraints. Evaluations across 10 state-of-the-art LLMs, including closed and open-source models, show that models can often select a plausible object, but fail to identify the correct parts, their affordances, and the underlying physical mechanism needed to solve the task, leading to a significant drop in performance. Furthermore, improvements from model scaling quickly saturate, strong general reasoning does not reliably translate to creative affordance discovery, and common inference-time strategies such as Chain-of-Thought yield limited gains. These results suggest that creative tool use remains a major challenge for current models, and that CreativityBench provides a useful testbed for studying this missing dimension of intelligence, with potential implications for planning and reasoning modules in future agents.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces CreativityBench, a benchmark for evaluating creative tool use in LLMs, built on a large-scale affordance knowledge base with 4K entities and 150K+ annotations. Evaluations across 10 state-of-the-art LLMs reveal that while models can select plausible objects, they struggle to identify the correct parts, affordances, and physical mechanisms, with model scaling, general reasoning, and inference-time strategies like Chain-of-Thought yielding limited gains.
AI.motivation: Creative problem-solving in LLMs, specifically through affordance-based creative tool use where models must repurpose objects based on non-obvious attributes and physical mechanisms, remains underexplored despite advances in reasoning and environment interaction.
AI.method: The authors constructed a large-scale affordance knowledge base (KB) with 4K entities and 150K+ annotations linking objects, parts, attributes, and actionable uses. From this KB, they generated 14K grounded reasoning tasks requiring non-obvious yet physically plausible solutions under constraints. They then evaluated 10 SOTA LLMs (both closed and open-source) on these tasks.
AI.result: LLMs can often select a plausible object but fail to identify the correct parts, their affordances, and the underlying physical mechanism needed, causing a significant performance drop. Model scaling quickly saturates, strong general reasoning does not reliably transfer to creative affordance discovery, and inference-time strategies like Chain-of-Thought provide limited improvements.
AI.conclusion: Creative tool use remains a major challenge for current LLMs. CreativityBench serves as a useful testbed for studying this missing dimension of intelligence, with implications for planning and reasoning modules in future agents.

title: RLDX-1 Technical Report
summary: While Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) have shown remarkable progress toward human-like generalist robotic policies through the versatile intelligence (i.e. broad scene understanding and language-conditioned generalization) inherited from pre-trained Vision-Language Models, they still struggle with complex real-world tasks requiring broader functional capabilities (e.g. motion awareness, memory-aware decision making, and physical sensing). To address this, we introduce RLDX-1, a general-purpose robotic policy for dexterous manipulation built on the Multi-Stream Action Transformer (MSAT), an architecture that unifies these capabilities by integrating heterogeneous modalities through modality-specific streams with cross-modal joint self-attention. RLDX-1 further combines this architecture with system-level design choices, including synthesizing training data for rare manipulation scenarios, learning procedures specialized for human-like manipulation, and inference optimizations for real-time deployment. Through empirical evaluation, we show that RLDX-1 consistently outperforms recent frontier VLAs (e.g. $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.6) across both simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks that require broad functional capabilities beyond general versatility. In particular, RLDX-1 shows superiority in ALLEX humanoid tasks by achieving success rates of 86.8% while $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.6 achieve around 40%, highlighting the ability of RLDX-1 to control a high-DoF humanoid robot under diverse functional demands. Together, these results position RLDX-1 as a promising step toward reliable VLAs for complex, contact-rich, and dynamic real-world dexterous manipulation.

AI.tldr: RLDX-1 is a general-purpose robotic policy for dexterous manipulation built on the Multi-Stream Action Transformer (MSAT), integrating heterogeneous modalities to address VLAs' limitations in motion awareness, memory-aware decision making, and physical sensing. It outperforms recent VLAs like π₀.₅ and GR00T N1.6, achieving 86.8% success rates on ALLEX humanoid tasks vs. ~40%.
AI.motivation: VLAs struggle with complex real-world tasks requiring broader functional capabilities beyond general versatility, such as motion awareness, memory-aware decision making, and physical sensing.
AI.method: Introduces Multi-Stream Action Transformer (MSAT) architecture with modality-specific streams and cross-modal joint self-attention, combined with system-level designs: synthetic data for rare scenarios, specialized learning procedures for human-like manipulation, and inference optimizations for real-time deployment.
AI.result: RLDX-1 consistently outperforms π₀.₅ and GR00T N1.6 in both simulation and real-world tasks requiring broad functional capabilities. On ALLEX humanoid tasks, RLDX-1 achieves 86.8% success rate vs. ~40% for baselines.
AI.conclusion: RLDX-1 represents a promising step toward reliable VLAs for complex, contact-rich, and dynamic real-world dexterous manipulation.

title: Stable Agentic Control: Tool-Mediated LLM Architecture for Autonomous Cyber Defense
comment: 23 pages total (9 main paper + 16 appendices/references), 2 figures
summary: Agentic systems involved in high-stake decision-making under adversarial pressure need formal guarantees not offered by existing approaches. Motivated by the operational needs of security operations centers (SOCs) that must configure endpoint detection and response (EDR) policies under adversarial pressure, we present a tool-mediated architecture: LLM agents use deterministic tools (Stackelberg best-response, Bayesian observer updates, attack-graph primitives) and select from finite action catalogs enforced at the tool-output interface. A composite Lyapunov function machine-checked in Lean 4 with zero sorry certifies controllability, observability from asymmetric sensor data, and Input-to-State Stability (ISS) robustness under intelligent adversarial disturbance, with two corollaries extending the certificate to any controller or adversary from the catalogs. On 282 real enterprise attack graphs, the claims hold with margin. On paired offensive/defensive telemetry, a tool-mediated Claude Sonnet 4 controller reduces the attacker's expected payoff (game value) by 59% relative to a deterministic greedy baseline, with zero variance across 40 runs at four temperatures. A Claude Haiku 4.5 controller converges to suboptimal game values but stays catalog-bounded over an additional 40 runs, demonstrating that architectural stability is not dependent on the controller capability. The LLM agent's non-determinism furthers creative exploration of strategies, while the tool-mediated architecture ensures system stability.

AI.tldr: A tool-mediated architecture using LLM agents with deterministic tools (Stackelberg game, Bayesian updates, attack graphs) and Lean 4-verified composite Lyapunov functions provides formal safety/stability guarantees for EDR policy configuration in SOCs under adversarial pressure, reducing attacker payoff by 59% with zero variance across runs.
AI.motivation: Agentic systems in high-stakes adversarial decision-making (e.g., SOC EDR policy configuration) lack formal guarantees that existing approaches cannot provide.
AI.method: Tool-mediated architecture: LLM agents use deterministic tools (Stackelberg best-response, Bayesian observer updates, attack-graph primitives) with finite action catalogs; a composite Lyapunov function machine-checked in Lean 4 certifies controllability, observability, and ISS robustness, with corollaries extending to any controller/adversary from the catalogs.
AI.result: On 282 real enterprise attack graphs, claims hold with margin. Claude Sonnet 4 controller reduces attacker's expected payoff by 59% vs. greedy baseline with zero variance across 40 runs at four temperatures. Claude Haiku 4.5 converges to suboptimal values but stays catalog-bounded, showing stability independent of controller capability.
AI.conclusion: The architecture ensures system stability via tool mediation while LLM non-determinism enables creative strategy exploration; formal guarantees are verified in Lean 4 with zero sorry.

title: Neural Control: Adjoint Learning Through Equilibrium Constraints
summary: Many physical AI tasks are governed by implicit equilibrium: an agent actuates a subset of degrees of freedom (boundary DoFs), while the remaining free DoFs settle by minimizing a total potential energy. Even seemingly basic tasks such as bending a deformable linear object (DLO) to a target shape can exhibit strongly nonlinear behavior due to multi-stability: the same boundary conditions may yield multiple equilibrium shapes depending on the actuation trajectory. However, learning and control in such systems is brittle because the actuation-to-configuration map is defined only implicitly, and naive backpropagation through iterative equilibrium solvers is memory- and compute-intensive. We propose Neural Control, a boundary-control framework that computes trajectory-dependent, memory-efficient proxy gradients by differentiating equilibrium conditions via an adjoint formulation, avoiding unrolling of solver iterations. To improve robustness over long horizons, we integrate these sensitivities into a receding-horizon MPC scheme that repeatedly re-anchors optimization to realized equilibria and mitigates basin-switching in multi-stable regimes. We evaluate Neural Control in simulation and on physical robots manipulating DLOs, and show improved performance over gradient-free baselines such as SPSA and CEM.

AI.tldr: A boundary-control framework called Neural Control that computes proxy gradients via adjoint formulation for tasks governed by implicit equilibrium, enabling trajectory-dependent, memory-efficient optimization for multi-stable physical systems like deformable linear objects.
AI.motivation: Learning and control in physical AI tasks with implicit equilibrium (e.g., bending deformable linear objects) is brittle because the actuation-to-configuration map is only implicitly defined, and naive backpropagation through iterative equilibrium solvers is memory- and compute-intensive.
AI.method: Neural Control computes trajectory-dependent, memory-efficient proxy gradients by differentiating equilibrium conditions via an adjoint formulation (avoiding unrolling of solver iterations), integrated into a receding-horizon MPC scheme that repeatedly re-anchors optimization to realized equilibria to mitigate basin-switching in multi-stable regimes.
AI.result: Evaluated in simulation and on physical robots manipulating deformable linear objects, showing improved performance over gradient-free baselines such as SPSA and CEM.
AI.conclusion: The proposed adjoint-based boundary-control framework enables efficient and robust control of multi-stable physical systems governed by implicit equilibrium, outperforming gradient-free methods.

title: Computing Thiele Rules on Interval Elections and their Generalizations
summary:
Approval-based committee voting has received significant attention in the social choice community. Among the studied rules, Thiele rules, and especially Proportional Approval Voting (PAV), stand out for desirable properties such as proportional representation, Pareto optimality, and support monotonicity. Their main drawback is that computing a Thiele outcome is NP-hard in general.
  A glimpse of hope comes from the fact that Thiele rules are better behaved under structured preferences. On the candidate interval (CI) domain, they are computable in polynomial time via a linear program (LP) that has a totally unimodular constraint matrix. Surprisingly, this approach fails for the related voter interval (VI) domain, and the complexity of the problem has repeatedly been posed as an open question. Our main result resolves this question: although the relevant matrix is not totally unimodular, the ``standard'' LP still admits at least one optimal integral solution, and we provide a fast algorithm for finding it.
  Our technique naturally extends to the voter-candidate interval (VCI) domain, also known as the 1-dimensional voter-candidate range (1D-VCR) domain, and to the linearly consistent (LC) domain, both of which generalize the candidate and voter interval domains. Although both the VCI and LC domains have been studied in social choice, their relationship was unknown. We show, through connections to graph theory, that LC strictly contains VCI. We also provide an alternative definition of LC that is closer in spirit to VCI and has a natural interpretation in approval elections; this equivalence may be of independent interest. Finally, we study an alternative tree-based generalization of VCI and show that Thiele rules become NP-hard to compute on this domain.

AI.tldr: Thiele rules (including PAV) are NP-hard in general but tractable on structured preference domains. The paper resolves the open question of tractability on the voter interval (VI) domain by showing the standard LP still yields integral optimal solutions, and provides a fast algorithm. It extends results to VCI and LC domains, establishes that LC strictly contains VCI, and shows NP-hardness on a tree-based generalization.
AI.motivation: While Thiele rules are desirable for properties like proportional representation and Pareto optimality, they are NP-hard to compute in general. Understanding their computational complexity on structured preference domains is crucial for practical applications.
AI.method: The paper uses linear programming with totally unimodular matrices for the candidate interval (CI) domain, then analyzes the voter interval (VI) domain by showing the standard LP admits integral optimal solutions despite non-total-unimodularity, providing a fast algorithm. It extends techniques to VCI and LC domains, uses graph theory to establish the containment relationship, and proves NP-hardness on a tree-based domain.
AI.result: Resolves the open complexity question for VI domain (polynomial-time solvable); shows LC strictly contains VCI; provides alternative definition of LC; demonstrates NP-hardness on a tree-based generalization.
AI.conclusion: Thiele rules are tractable on interval-based and linearly consistent domains, but become NP-hard on tree-based generalizations, delineating the boundary between tractable and intractable preference structures.

title: Making the Invisible Visible: Understanding the Mismatch Between Organizational Goals and Worker Experiences in AI Adoption
summary: While AI is often introduced into organizations to drive innovation and efficiency, many adoption efforts fail as workers resist and struggle to integrate these systems. These failures point to a deeper issue: workers, the very people expected to collaborate with AI, are often invisible in decisions about how AI is designed and used. Drawing on interviews with professionals who interact with AI systems daily in healthcare, finance, and management, we examine the disconnect between organizational expectations and worker experiences. We identify key barriers, including poor usability and interoperability, misaligned expectations, limited control, and insufficient communication. These challenges highlight a gap between how organizations implement AI and the evolving worker needs, tasks, and workflows that it fails to support. We argue that successful adoption requires recognizing workers as central to AI integration and propose adaptation strategies at the individual, task, and organizational levels to better align AI systems with real-world practices.

AI.tldr: Workers are often excluded from AI adoption decisions, leading to resistance and failure. Based on interviews across healthcare, finance, and management, the paper identifies barriers like poor usability, misaligned expectations, limited control, and insufficient communication, and proposes worker-centered adaptation strategies at individual, task, and organizational levels.
AI.motivation: Despite the promise of AI to drive innovation and efficiency in organizations, many AI adoption efforts fail due to worker resistance and struggle, highlighting that workers—who are expected to collaborate with AI—are often invisible in decisions about AI design and implementation.
AI.method: Qualitative interviews with professionals who interact with AI systems daily in healthcare, finance, and management, examining the disconnect between organizational expectations and worker experiences.
AI.result: Identified key barriers: poor usability and interoperability, misaligned expectations, limited control, and insufficient communication. These reveal a gap between how organizations implement AI and the evolving worker needs, tasks, and workflows that the AI fails to support.
AI.conclusion: Successful AI adoption requires recognizing workers as central to AI integration. Worker-centered adaptation strategies at individual, task, and organizational levels are needed to better align AI systems with real-world practices.

title: Height Control and Optimal Torque Planning for Jumping With Wheeled-Bipedal Robots
comment: 6 pages, 16 figures. Accepted for publication at ICARM 2021
summary: This paper mainly studies the accurate height jumping control of wheeled-bipedal robots based on torque planning and energy consumption optimization. Due to the characteristics of underactuated, nonlinear estimation, and instantaneous impact in the jumping process, accurate control of the wheeled-bipedal robot's jumping height is complicated. In reality, robots often jump at excessive height to ensure safety, causing additional motor loss, greater ground reaction force and more energy consumption. To solve this problem, a novel wheeled-bipedal jumping dynamical model(W-JBD) is proposed to achieve accurate height control. It performs well but not suitable for the real robot because the torque has a striking step. Therefore, the Bayesian optimization for torque planning method(BOTP) is proposed, which can obtain the optimal torque planning without accurate dynamic model and within few iterations. BOTP method can reduce 82.3% height error, 26.9% energy cost with continuous torque curve. This result is validated in the Webots simulation platform. Based on the torque curve obtained in the W-JBD model to narrow the searching space, BOTP can quickly converge (40 times on average). Cooperating W-JBD model and BOTP method, it is possible to achieve the height control of real robots with reasonable times of experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a wheeled-bipedal jumping dynamical model (W-JBD) and a Bayesian optimization for torque planning method (BOTP) to achieve accurate height jumping control of wheeled-bipedal robots. The BOTP method reduces height error by 82.3% and energy cost by 26.9% with continuous torque curves, validated in Webots simulation.
AI.motivation: Accurate height jumping control of wheeled-bipedal robots is complicated due to underactuation, nonlinear estimation, and instantaneous impact. Existing methods often result in excessive jumping height to ensure safety, causing additional motor loss, greater ground reaction force, and higher energy consumption.
AI.method: First, a wheeled-bipedal jumping dynamical model (W-JBD) is proposed for accurate height control. However, its torque output has sharp steps unsuitable for real robots. Thus, a Bayesian optimization for torque planning method (BOTP) is introduced, which uses the torque curve from W-JBD to narrow the search space and finds optimal torque planning without requiring an accurate dynamic model, converging in ~40 iterations on average.
AI.result: BOTP reduces height error by 82.3% and energy cost by 26.9% with a continuous torque curve, validated in the Webots simulation platform. The method converges quickly (40 iterations on average) by leveraging the W-JBD model to narrow the search space.
AI.conclusion: Cooperating W-JBD model and BOTP method makes it possible to achieve accurate height control of real wheeled-bipedal robots with a reasonable number of experiments.

title: Programmatic Context Augmentation for LLM-based Symbolic Regression
summary: Symbolic regression (SR), the task of discovering mathematical expressions that best describe a given dataset, remains a fundamental challenge in scientific discovery. Traditional approaches, primarily based on genetic algorithms and related evolutionary methods, have proven useful but suffer from scalability and expressivity limitations. Recently, large language model (LLM)-based evolutionary search methods have been introduced into SR and show promise. However, existing LLM-based approaches typically rely on scalar evaluation metrics, such as mean squared error, as the sole source of feedback during the search process, thereby overlooking the rich information embedded in the dataset. To address this limitation, we propose a novel LLM-based evolutionary search framework that incorporates programmatic context augmentation. By enabling code-based interactions with the dataset, our method can actively perform data analysis and extract informative signals, beyond aggregated evaluation scores. We evaluate our framework on advanced benchmarks, such as LLM-SRBench, and demonstrate superior efficiency and accuracy compared to strong baselines.

AI.tldr: A novel LLM-based evolutionary symbolic regression framework that uses programmatic context augmentation to extract richer information from datasets beyond simple scalar metrics, demonstrating superior performance on benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing LLM-based symbolic regression methods rely solely on scalar evaluation metrics (e.g., MSE) as feedback, overlooking rich information embedded in datasets.
AI.method: An LLM-based evolutionary search framework with programmatic context augmentation that enables code-based interactions with datasets for active data analysis and informative signal extraction.
AI.result: Superior efficiency and accuracy compared to strong baselines on advanced benchmarks like LLM-SRBench.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating programmatic context augmentation into LLM-based evolutionary search significantly improves symbolic regression performance by leveraging richer dataset information beyond aggregated scores.

title: Learning Reactive Dexterous Grasping via Hierarchical Task-Space RL Planning and Joint-Space QP Control
summary: In this work, we propose a hybrid hierarchical control framework for reactive dexterous grasping that explicitly decouples high-level spatial intent from low-level joint execution. We introduce a multi-agent reinforcement learning architecture, specialized into distinct arm and hand agents, that acts as a high-level planner by generating desired task-space velocity commands. These commands are then processed by a GPU-parallelized quadratic programming controller, which translates them into feasible joint velocities while strictly enforcing kinematic limits and collision avoidance. This structural isolation not only accelerates training convergence but also strictly enforces hardware safety. Furthermore, the architecture unlocks zero-shot steerability, allowing system operators to dynamically adjust safety margins and avoid dynamic obstacles without retraining the policy. We extensively validate the proposed framework through a rigorous simulation-to-reality pipeline. Real-world hardware experiments on a 7-DoF arm equipped with a 20-DoF anthropomorphic hand demonstrate highly robust zero-shot transferability for dexterous grasping to a diverse set of unseen objects, highlighting the system's ability to reactively recover from unexpected physical disturbances in unstructured environments.

AI.tldr: A hybrid hierarchical control framework for reactive dexterous grasping that decouples high-level spatial intent from low-level joint execution, using multi-agent RL for high-level planning and GPU-parallelized QP control for low-level execution, achieving zero-shot steerability and robust sim-to-real transfer on a 7-DoF arm + 20-DoF hand.
AI.motivation: To enable reactive dexterous grasping that is both safe (kinematic limits, collision avoidance) and steerable (dynamic adjustment of safety margins/obstacles without retraining), while overcoming training convergence issues in end-to-end grasping policies.
AI.method: Hybrid hierarchical control: (1) high-level multi-agent RL (separate arm & hand agents) generates task-space velocity commands; (2) low-level GPU-parallelized quadratic programming (QP) controller translates commands to feasible joint velocities under kinematic and collision constraints.
AI.result: Accelerated training convergence, strict hardware safety enforcement, zero-shot steerability. Real-world experiments on 7-DoF arm + 20-DoF anthropomorphic hand show robust zero-shot sim-to-real transfer and reactive recovery from physical disturbances on diverse unseen objects.
AI.conclusion: The structural decoupling of spatial intent from joint execution enables safe, steerable, and transferable dexterous grasping, validated through rigorous sim-to-real hardware experiments.

title: BifrostUMI: Bridging Robot-Free Demonstrations and Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation
summary: High-quality data collection is a fundamental cornerstone for training humanoid whole-body visuomotor policies. Current data acquisition paradigms predominantly rely on robot teleoperation, which is often hindered by limited hardware accessibility and low operational efficiency. Inspired by the Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI), we propose BifrostUMI, a portable, efficient, and robot-free data collection framework tailored for humanoid robots. BifrostUMI leverages lightweight VR devices to capture human demonstrations as sparse keypoint trajectories while simultaneously recording wrist-mounted visual data. These multimodal data are subsequently utilized to train a high-level policy network that predicts future keypoint trajectories conditioned on the captured visual features. Through a robust keypoint retargeting pipeline, keypoint trajectories are precisely mapped onto the robot's morphology and executed via a whole-body controller. This approach enables the seamless transfer of diverse and agile behaviors from natural human demonstrations to humanoid embodiments. We demonstrate the efficacy and versatility of the proposed framework across two distinct experimental scenarios.

AI.tldr: BifrostUMI is a portable, robot-free data collection framework for humanoid robots that uses VR devices to capture human demonstrations as sparse keypoint trajectories and wrist-mounted visual data, enabling seamless transfer of diverse behaviors to humanoid embodiments via a keypoint retargeting pipeline and whole-body controller.
AI.motivation: High-quality data collection for humanoid whole-body visuomotor policies is currently hindered by robot teleoperation's limited hardware accessibility and low operational efficiency.
AI.method: BifrostUMI uses lightweight VR devices to capture human demonstrations as sparse keypoint trajectories with wrist-mounted visual data, trains a high-level policy network to predict future keypoints conditioned on visual features, then maps keypoints to the robot via a retargeting pipeline and executes with a whole-body controller.
AI.result: Demonstrated efficacy and versatility across two distinct experimental scenarios, enabling transfer of diverse and agile behaviors from natural human demonstrations to humanoid embodiments.
AI.conclusion: BifrostUMI provides an efficient, portable, robot-free alternative to teleoperation for collecting high-quality training data for humanoid whole-body visuomotor policies.

title: Learning Correct Behavior from Examples: Validating Sequential Execution in Autonomous Agents
summary: As autonomous agents become increasingly sophisticated, validating their sequential behavior presents a significant challenge. Traditional testing approaches require manual specification, exact sequence matching, or thousands of training examples. We present a novel algorithm that automatically learns correct behavior from just 2-10 passing execution traces and validates new executions against this learned model. Our approach combines dominator analysis from compiler theory with multimodal large language model-powered semantic understanding to identify essential states and handle non-deterministic behavior. The system constructs a generalized ground truth model using Prefix Tree Acceptors, merges traces through multi-tiered equivalence detection, and validates new executions via topological subsequence matching. In controlled experiments, our system achieved high accuracy in detecting product bugs and false successes using only 3 training traces. This approach provides explainable validation results with coverage metrics and works across diverse domains including UI testing, code generation, and robotic processes.

AI.tldr: A novel algorithm that automatically learns correct agent behavior from just 2-10 passing traces using dominator analysis and multimodal LLMs, then validates new executions via topological subsequence matching.
AI.motivation: Validating sequential behavior of autonomous agents is challenging because traditional approaches require manual specification, exact sequence matching, or thousands of training examples.
AI.method: Combines dominator analysis from compiler theory with multimodal LLM-powered semantic understanding. Uses Prefix Tree Acceptors to construct generalized ground truth models, merges traces via multi-tiered equivalence detection, and validates executions through topological subsequence matching.
AI.result: Achieved high accuracy in detecting product bugs and false successes using only 3 training traces in controlled experiments.
AI.conclusion: Provides explainable validation results with coverage metrics and works across diverse domains including UI testing, code generation, and robotic processes, requiring minimal training data.

title: Bridging the Embodiment Gap: Disentangled Cross-Embodiment Video Editing
summary: Learning robotic manipulation from human videos is a promising solution to the data bottleneck in robotics, but the distribution shift between humans and robots remains a critical challenge. Existing approaches often produce entangled representations, where task-relevant information is coupled with human-specific kinematics, limiting their adaptability. We propose a generative framework for cross-embodiment video editing that directly addresses this by learning explicitly disentangled task and embodiment representations. Our method factorizes a demonstration video into two orthogonal latent spaces by enforcing a dual contrastive objective: it minimizes mutual information between the spaces to ensure independence while maximizing intra-space consistency to create stable representations. A parameter-efficient adapter injects these latent codes into a frozen video diffusion model, enabling the synthesis of a coherent robot execution video from a single human demonstration, without requiring paired cross-embodiment data. Experiments show our approach generates temporally consistent and morphologically accurate robot demonstrations, offering a scalable solution to leverage internet-scale human video for robot learning.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a generative framework that uses disentangled task and embodiment representations to edit human demonstration videos into robot execution videos, enabling scalable robot learning from human video data without paired cross-embodiment data.
AI.motivation: Learning robotic manipulation from human videos faces a distribution shift between humans and robots; existing approaches produce entangled representations coupling task-relevant information with human-specific kinematics, limiting adaptability across embodiments.
AI.method: The method factorizes a demonstration video into two orthogonal latent spaces (task and embodiment) using a dual contrastive objective that minimizes mutual information for independence while maximizing intra-space consistency. A parameter-efficient adapter injects these latent codes into a frozen video diffusion model to synthesize robot execution videos from a single human demonstration.
AI.result: The approach generates temporally consistent and morphologically accurate robot demonstrations, and operates without requiring paired cross-embodiment data during training.
AI.conclusion: The proposed disentangled representation learning framework offers a scalable solution for leveraging internet-scale human video data for robot learning by directly addressing the cross-embodiment distribution shift.

title: Terminus-4B: Can a Smaller Model Replace Frontier LLMs at Agentic Execution Tasks?
summary: Modern coding agents increasingly delegate specialized subtasks to subagents, which are smaller, focused agentic loops that handle narrow responsibilities like search, debugging or terminal execution. This architectural pattern keeps the main agent's context window clean by isolating verbose outputs (e.g. build logs, test results, etc.) within the subagent context. Typically when agents employ subagents for such tasks, they use frontier models as these subagents. In this paper, we investigate whether a finetuned small language model (SLM) can achieve comparable performance to frontier models in the task of agentic terminal execution. We present Terminus-4B, which is a post-trained Qwen3-4B model via Supervised Finetuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) using rubric-based LLM-as-judge reward, specifically for this task. In our extensive evaluation spanning various frontier models, training ablations and main agent configurations, we find that Terminus-4B is able to reduce the token usage of the main agent by up to ~30% compared to the No Subagent baseline with no impact to agent performance on benchmarks like SWE-Bench Pro and our internal SWE-Bench C# benchmark, which tends to be heavy in verbose execution tasks. Furthermore, Terminus-4B improves key metrics showing the main agent relying on the outputs of the subagent and doing fewer terminal execution tasks by itself. We see that our model not only closes the gap between the Vanilla Qwen model and frontier models like Claude Sonnet / Opus / GPT-5.3-Codex, but often even exceeds their performance.

AI.tldr: Terminus-4B, a finetuned 4B-parameter SLM, achieves comparable or superior performance to frontier models for agentic terminal execution subagents, reducing main agent token usage by ~30% without performance loss on SWE-Bench benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Modern coding agents delegate specialized subtasks to subagents to keep the main agent's context clean. Frontier models are typically used as subagents, but this work investigates whether a finetuned small language model can match frontier model performance in agentic terminal execution.
AI.method: Post-trained Qwen3-4B via Supervised Finetuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) using rubric-based LLM-as-judge reward, specifically for terminal execution subagent tasks. Evaluated against frontier models across various training ablations and main agent configurations.
AI.result: Terminus-4B reduces main agent token usage by ~30% compared to No Subagent baseline with no performance degradation on SWE-Bench Pro and internal SWE-Bench C# benchmarks. It improves key metrics showing the main agent relies on subagent outputs and performs fewer terminal tasks itself. It closes and often exceeds the gap between Vanilla Qwen and frontier models like Claude Sonnet/Opus/GPT-5.3-Codex.
AI.conclusion: A finetuned SLM can effectively replace frontier models as terminal execution subagents, achieving better efficiency (token reduction) while maintaining or exceeding task performance, enabling more cost-effective agentic systems.

title: Jiao: Bridging Isolation and Customization in Mixed Criticality Robotics
comment: Accepted by Infocom'26 Embodied Intelligence Networks workshop
summary: Consumer robotics demands consolidation of safety-critical control, perception pipelines, and user applications on shared multicore platforms. While static partitioning hypervisors provide hardware-enforced isolation, directly transplanting automotive architectures encounters an expertise asymmetry problem in which end-users modifying robot behavior lack the systems knowledge that platform developers possess. We present an architecture addressing this challenge through three integrated components. A Safe IO Cell provides hardware-level override capability. A Parameter Synchronization Service encapsulates cross-domain complexity. A Safety Communication Layer implements IEC~61508-aligned verification. Our empirical evaluation on an ARM Cortex-A55 platform demonstrates that partition isolation reduces cycle-period jitter by 84.5\% and cuts tail timing error by nearly an order of magnitude (p99 $|$jitter$|$ from 69.0\,$μ$s to 7.8\,$μ$s), eliminating all $>$50\,$μ$s~excursions.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an architecture for consumer robotics that combines a Safe IO Cell, Parameter Synchronization Service, and Safety Communication Layer to address the expertise asymmetry between platform developers and end-users. Evaluated on ARM Cortex-A55, the approach reduces cycle-period jitter by 84.5% and p99 tail timing error from 69.0μs to 7.8μs, eliminating all >50μs excursions.
AI.motivation: Consumer robotics requires consolidating safety-critical control, perception, and user applications on shared multicore platforms. While static partitioning hypervisors offer hardware-enforced isolation, directly applying automotive architectures creates an expertise asymmetry problem: end-users modifying robot behavior lack the systems knowledge that platform developers possess.
AI.method: Three integrated components: (1) Safe IO Cell providing hardware-level override, (2) Parameter Synchronization Service encapsulating cross-domain complexity, (3) Safety Communication Layer implementing IEC~61508-aligned verification.
AI.result: On ARM Cortex-A55, partition isolation reduces cycle-period jitter by 84.5%, cuts p99 |jitter| from 69.0μs to 7.8μs (nearly an order of magnitude), and eliminates all >50μs excursions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed architecture effectively bridges the expertise gap in consumer robotics by providing hardware-enforced isolation with accessible interfaces, achieving significant timing determinism improvements without requiring end-users to have deep systems expertise.

title: Stop Automating Peer Review Without Rigorous Evaluation
summary: Large language models offer a tempting solution to address the peer review crisis. This position paper argues that today's AI systems should not be used to produce paper reviews. We ground this position in an empirical comparison of human- versus AI-generated ICLR 2026 reviews and an evaluation of the effect of automated paper rewriting on different AI reviewers. We identify two critical issues: 1) AI reviewers exhibit a hivemind effect of excessive agreement within and across papers that reduces perspective diversity. 2) AI review scores are trivially gameable through paper laundering: prompting an LLM to rewrite a paper could significantly increase the scores from AI reviewers, demonstrating that LLM reviewers are easy to game through stylistic changes rather than scientific results. However, non-gameability and review diversity are necessary but not sufficient conditions for automation. We argue that addressing the peer review crisis requires a science of peer review automation -- not general-purpose LLMs deployed without rigorous evaluation.

AI.tldr: This position paper argues against using LLMs for peer review, showing empirically that AI reviewers suffer from a hivemind effect (excessive agreement reducing diversity) and are trivially gameable via paper laundering (stylistic rewriting inflates scores). The authors advocate for a science of peer review automation rather than deploying general-purpose LLMs without rigorous evaluation.
AI.motivation: To address whether LLMs can be responsibly used to automate peer review, given the growing peer review crisis and the temptation to deploy LLMs as a quick fix.
AI.method: Empirical comparison of human-generated vs. AI-generated ICLR 2026 reviews, plus evaluation of automated paper rewriting (paper laundering) on different AI reviewers.
AI.result: Two critical issues identified: (1) AI reviewers exhibit a hivemind effect—excessive agreement within and across papers, reducing perspective diversity. (2) AI review scores are easily gameable via paper laundering—prompting an LLM to rewrite a paper significantly inflates scores from AI reviewers through stylistic changes rather than scientific merit.
AI.conclusion: Non-gameability and review diversity are necessary but not sufficient for automation. Addressing the peer review crisis requires a dedicated science of peer review automation, not deploying general-purpose LLMs without rigorous evaluation.

title: Feasibility-aware Hybrid Control for Motion Planning under Signal Temporal Logics
summary: In this work, a novel method for planar task and motion planning based on hybrid modeling is proposed. By virtue of a discrete variable which models local constraint satisfaction and enables local feasibility analysis, the proposed control architecture unifies planning with control design. Concurrently, control barrier functions are designed on a transformed disk version of the original nonconvex and geometrically complex robotic workspace, thus amending the issue of deadlocks. Simulations of the proposed method indicate effective handling of multiple overlapping spatio-temporal tasks even in the face of input saturation.

AI.tldr: A novel hybrid modeling method for planar task and motion planning is proposed, using discrete variables for local feasibility analysis and control barrier functions on a transformed disk workspace to handle deadlocks, with simulations showing effective management of overlapping spatio-temporal tasks under input saturation.
AI.motivation: To address the challenges of planar task and motion planning, including nonconvex and geometrically complex workspaces, deadlock issues, and handling multiple overlapping spatio-temporal tasks under input saturation.
AI.method: Hybrid modeling approach with a discrete variable for local constraint satisfaction and feasibility analysis; control barrier functions designed on a transformed disk version of the original workspace to resolve deadlocks.
AI.result: Simulations demonstrate effective handling of multiple overlapping spatio-temporal tasks even with input saturation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed hybrid control architecture successfully unifies planning with control design and resolves deadlock issues in complex planar task and motion planning scenarios.

title: ADAPTS: Agentic Decomposition for Automated Protocol-agnostic Tracking of Symptoms
summary: Modeling latent clinical constructs from unconstrained clinical interactions is a unique challenge in affective computing. We present ADAPTS (Agentic Decomposition for Automated Protocol-agnostic Tracking of Symptoms), a framework for automated rating of depression and anxiety severity using a mixture-of-agents LLM architecture. This approach decomposes long-form clinical interviews into symptom-specific reasoning tasks, producing auditable justifications while preserving temporal and speaker alignment. Generalization was evaluated across two independent datasets ($N=204$) with distinct interview structures. On high-discrepancy interviews, automated ratings approximated expert benchmarks ($\text{absolute error}=22$) more closely than original human ratings ($\text{absolute error}=26$). Implementing an ``extended'' protocol that incorporates qualitative clinical conventions significantly stabilized ratings, with absolute agreement reaching $\text{ICC(2,1)} = 0.877$. These findings suggest that the ADAPTS framework enables promising evaluations of psychiatric severity. While the current implementation is purely text-based, the underlying architecture is readily extensible to multimodal inputs, including acoustic and visual features. By approximating expert-level precision in a protocol-agnostic manner, this framework provides a foundation for objective and scalable psychiatric assessment, especially in resource-limited settings.

AI.tldr: ADAPTS is a mixture-of-agents LLM framework that decomposes clinical interviews into symptom-specific reasoning tasks to automatically rate depression and anxiety severity, achieving near-expert precision (ICC=0.877) across diverse interview protocols.
AI.motivation: Modeling latent clinical constructs from unconstrained clinical interactions is a unique challenge in affective computing, motivating the need for automated, protocol-agnostic psychiatric assessment.
AI.method: ADAPTS uses a mixture-of-agents LLM architecture to decompose long-form clinical interviews into symptom-specific reasoning tasks, preserving temporal and speaker alignment, and includes an "extended" protocol incorporating qualitative clinical conventions.
AI.result: On high-discrepancy interviews, ADAPTS achieved lower absolute error (22) than original human ratings (26). With the extended protocol, absolute agreement reached ICC(2,1)=0.877 across two datasets (N=204) with distinct interview structures.
AI.conclusion: ADAPTS enables promising, auditable, and scalable evaluations of psychiatric severity in a protocol-agnostic manner, with the architecture readily extensible to multimodal inputs for use in resource-limited settings.

title: Sensorless State Estimation and Control for Agile Cable-Suspended Payload Transport by Quadrotors
summary: This work proposes a novel control and estimation approach for aerial manipulation of a cable-suspended load using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). Common approaches in the state of the art have practical limitations, relying on direct load measurements and Lagrangian methods for dynamic modeling. The lack of a straightforward dynamic model of the system led us to propose adopting the Udwadia-Kalaba method to explicitly incorporate the cable's geometric constraints. This formulation allowed for the consistent derivation of the tension force and its direct integration into the NMPC prediction model. Additionally, we propose a sensorless load state estimation based on the same geometric constraints. Results from real-robot experiments demonstrated that the explicit inclusion of load dynamics in the optimization problem significantly reduces trajectory-tracking errors and yields better overall performance compared to strategies based on incomplete models.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a UAV-based aerial manipulation system for cable-suspended loads that uses the Udwadia-Kalaba method to explicitly model cable constraints, integrates tension forces into an NMPC prediction model, and employs sensorless geometric-constraint-based load state estimation, achieving reduced tracking errors in real-robot experiments.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches for aerial manipulation of cable-suspended loads suffer from practical limitations such as reliance on direct load measurements and complex Lagrangian dynamic modeling, lacking a straightforward dynamic model of the system.
AI.method: Adopts the Udwadia-Kalaba method to explicitly incorporate cable geometric constraints, enabling consistent derivation of tension force and direct integration into the NMPC (Nonlinear Model Predictive Control) prediction model; proposes sensorless load state estimation based on the same geometric constraints.
AI.result: Real-robot experiments showed that explicit inclusion of load dynamics in the optimization significantly reduces trajectory-tracking errors and yields better overall performance compared to strategies based on incomplete models.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Udwadia-Kalaba-based control and sensorless estimation framework outperforms incomplete-model approaches for UAV cable-suspended load manipulation.

title: Evaluating Prompting and Execution-Based Methods for Deterministic Computation in LLMs
comment: 8 pages, 1 figure. Code and dataset available at https://github.com/bigbird231/llm-exact-computation-dataset
summary:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in natural language understanding and reasoning. However, their ability to perform exact, deterministic computation remains unclear. In this work, we systematically evaluate multiple prompting strategies, including Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Least-to-Most decomposition, Program-of-Thought (PoT), and Self-Consistency (SC), on tasks requiring precise and error-free outputs, including binary counting, longest substring detection, and arithmetic evaluation.
  To support this study, we introduce a synthetic dataset with diverse natural language instructions, enabling controlled evaluation of exact computation across multiple task types.
  Our results show that standard prompting methods achieve only moderate accuracy on sequence-based tasks. CoT provides limited improvement, while Least-to-Most suffers from error accumulation. In contrast, PoT achieves perfect accuracy by generating executable code and delegating computation to an external interpreter. Self-Consistency improves robustness through majority voting, but incurs substantial computational overhead.
  We further train a small domain-specific model (CodeT5-small) to generate executable programs, which achieves perfect accuracy on held-out synthetic test data across all tasks with minimal training cost.
  Overall, our findings suggest that LLMs may simulate reasoning patterns rather than reliably perform exact symbolic computation. For deterministic tasks, combining LLMs with external tools or using specialized models provides a more reliable and efficient solution.

AI.tldr: LLMs struggle with exact deterministic computation tasks; while standard prompting methods yield moderate accuracy, Program-of-Thought (PoT) and a small fine-tuned CodeT5-small model achieve perfect accuracy by delegating computation to external code execution, suggesting LLMs simulate reasoning rather than perform precise symbolic computation.
AI.motivation: To systematically evaluate whether LLMs can reliably perform exact, deterministic computation (e.g., binary counting, substring detection, arithmetic) rather than only natural language understanding and reasoning, and to identify effective prompting strategies for such tasks.
AI.method: Systematically compared Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Least-to-Most decomposition, Program-of-Thought (PoT), and Self-Consistency (SC) on exact computation tasks using a synthetic dataset with diverse natural language instructions; additionally, fine-tuned CodeT5-small to generate executable programs.
AI.result: Standard prompting achieves only moderate accuracy. CoT yields limited gains; Least-to-Most suffers error accumulation. PoT achieves perfect accuracy by delegating to an external interpreter. Self-Consistency improves robustness but with high overhead. Fine-tuned CodeT5-small achieves perfect accuracy on held-out synthetic data with minimal training cost.
AI.conclusion: LLMs may simulate reasoning rather than reliably perform exact symbolic computation. For deterministic tasks, combining LLMs with external tools or using specialized small models provides a more reliable and efficient solution.

title: FUS3DMaps: Scalable and Accurate Open-Vocabulary Semantic Mapping by 3D Fusion of Voxel- and Instance-Level Layers
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: Open-vocabulary semantic mapping enables robots to spatially ground previously unseen concepts without requiring predefined class sets. Current training-free methods commonly rely on multi-view fusion of semantic embeddings into a 3D map, either at the instance-level via segmenting views and encoding image crops of segments, or by projecting image patch embeddings directly into a dense semantic map. The latter approach sidesteps segmentation and 2D-to-3D instance association by operating on full uncropped image frames, but existing methods remain limited in scalability. We present FUS3DMaps, an online dual-layer semantic mapping method that jointly maintains both dense and instance-level open-vocabulary layers within a shared voxel map. This design enables further voxel-level semantic fusion of the layer embeddings, combining the complementary strengths of both semantic mapping approaches. We find that our proposed semantic cross-layer fusion approach improves the quality of both the instance-level and dense layers, while also enabling a scalable and highly accurate instance-level map where the dense layer and cross-layer fusion are restricted to a spatial sliding window. Experiments on established 3D semantic segmentation benchmarks as well as a selection of large-scale scenes show that FUS3DMaps achieves accurate open-vocabulary semantic mapping at multi-story building scales. Additional material and code will be made available: https://githanonymous.github.io/FUS3DMaps/.

AI.tldr: FUS3DMaps is an online dual-layer open-vocabulary semantic mapping method that jointly maintains dense and instance-level layers in a shared voxel map, using cross-layer fusion to improve both layers' quality and enable scalable, accurate mapping at building scale.
AI.motivation: Existing training-free open-vocabulary semantic mapping methods either use instance-level fusion (segmenting views + encoding crops) or dense patch embedding projection. The dense approach avoids segmentation and 2D-to-3D association but lacks scalability. Neither approach fully leverages the complementary strengths of both paradigms.
AI.method: FUS3DMaps maintains a shared voxel map with two layers: (1) a dense layer from full uncropped image patch embeddings, and (2) an instance-level layer from segmented regions. Cross-layer fusion combines voxel-level semantic embeddings from both layers. To maintain scalability, the dense layer and cross-layer fusion are restricted to a spatial sliding window, while the instance-level map scales globally.
AI.result: FUS3DMaps achieves accurate open-vocabulary semantic mapping on established 3D semantic segmentation benchmarks and large-scale multi-story building scenes, outperforming existing methods in both accuracy and scalability.
AI.conclusion: Cross-layer fusion between dense and instance-level semantic embeddings improves both layers' quality and enables scalable, building-scale open-vocabulary mapping without predefined class sets.

title: cotomi Act: Learning to Automate Work by Watching You
summary: What if a browser agent could learn your work simply by watching you do it? We present cotomi Act, a browser-based computer-using agent that combines reliable multi-step task execution with persistent organizational knowledge learned from user behavior. For execution, an agent scaffold with adaptive lazy observation, verbal-diff-based history compression, coarse-grained actions, and test-time scaling via best-of-N action selection achieves 80.4% on the 179-task WebArena human-evaluation subset, exceeding the reported 78.2% human baseline. For organizational knowledge, a behavior-to-knowledge pipeline passively observes the user's browsing and progressively abstracts it into artifacts (task boards, wiki) exposed through a shared workspace editable by both user and agent. A controlled proxy evaluation confirms that task success improves as behavior-derived knowledge accumulates. In our live demonstration, attendees interact with the system in a real browser, issuing tasks and observing end-to-end autonomous execution and shared knowledge management.

AI.tldr: cotomi Act is a browser agent that learns from watching users, combining autonomous task execution (80.4% on WebArena, exceeding human baseline) with persistent organizational knowledge extracted from user behavior via a behavior-to-knowledge pipeline, achieving improved task success as knowledge accumulates.
AI.motivation: To enable browser agents to acquire persistent organizational knowledge by passively observing user behavior, overcoming the limitation that current agents lack long-term learning from human demonstrations.
AI.method: 1) An agent scaffold with adaptive lazy observation, verbal-diff-based history compression, coarse-grained actions, and test-time scaling via best-of-N action selection. 2) A behavior-to-knowledge pipeline that passively observes browsing and abstracts it into artifacts (task boards, wiki) in a shared workspace editable by both user and agent.
AI.result: 80.4% success rate on the 179-task WebArena human-evaluation subset, exceeding the reported 78.2% human baseline. Task success improves as behavior-derived knowledge accumulates (validated via controlled proxy evaluation).
AI.conclusion: A browser agent can both execute tasks autonomously at super-human levels and continuously learn organizational knowledge from passive observation of user behavior, with shared knowledge management enabling progressive improvement.

title: Robust Visual SLAM for UAV Navigation in GPS-Denied and Degraded Environments: A Multi-Paradigm Evaluation and Deployment Study
summary: Reliable localization in GPS-denied, visually degraded environments is critical for autonomous UAV opera- tions. This paper presents a systematic comparative evaluation of five V-SLAM systems ORB-SLAM3, DPVO, DROID-SLAM, DUSt3R, and MASt3R spanning classical, deep learning, recurrent, and Vision Transformer (ViT) paradigms. Experiments are conducted on curated sequences from four public benchmarks (TUM RGB-D, EuRoC MAV, UMA-VI, SubT-MRS) and a custom monocular indoor dataset under five controlled degradation conditions (normal, low light, dust haze, motion blur, and combined), with sub-millimeter Vicon ground truth. Results show that ORB-SLAM3 fails critically under severe degradation (62.4% overall TSR; 0% under dense haze), while learning-based methods remain robust: MASt3R achieves the lowest degraded ATE (0.027 m) and DUSt3R the highest tracking success (96.5%). DPVO offers the best efficiency robustness trade-off (18.6 FPS, 3.1 GB GPU memory, 86.1% TSR), making it the preferred choice for memory-constrained embedded platforms. Embedded deployment analysis across NVIDIA Jetson platforms provides actionable guidelines for SLAM selection under SWaP-constrained UAV scenarios.

AI.tldr: Comparative evaluation of five V-SLAM systems (ORB-SLAM3, DPVO, DROID-SLAM, DUSt3R, MASt3R) across degraded visual conditions, finding learning-based methods outperform classical SLAM, with MASt3R best in accuracy (ATE 0.027m), DUSt3R best in tracking success (96.5%), and DPVO best efficiency-robustness trade-off (18.6 FPS, 3.1 GB, 86.1% TSR) for embedded UAV deployment.
AI.motivation: Reliable localization in GPS-denied, visually degraded environments is critical for autonomous UAV operations, yet no systematic comparison of diverse V-SLAM paradigms under controlled degradation existed.
AI.method: Five V-SLAM systems spanning classical (ORB-SLAM3), deep learning (DPVO), recurrent (DROID-SLAM), and ViT (DUSt3R, MASt3R) paradigms were evaluated on curated sequences from four public benchmarks plus a custom monocular indoor dataset under five controlled degradation conditions (normal, low light, dust haze, motion blur, combined) with sub-millimeter Vicon ground truth. Embedded deployment analysis conducted on NVIDIA Jetson platforms.
AI.result: ORB-SLAM3 fails critically under severe degradation (62.4% overall TSR; 0% under dense haze). MASt3R achieves lowest degraded ATE (0.027 m), DUSt3R highest tracking success (96.5%). DPVO offers best efficiency-robustness trade-off (18.6 FPS, 3.1 GB GPU memory, 86.1% TSR).
AI.conclusion: Learning-based methods are more robust than classical SLAM under degradation; DPVO is preferred for memory-constrained embedded platforms; actionable guidelines for SLAM selection under SWaP-constrained UAV scenarios are provided.

title: Enhancing Agent Safety Judgment: Controlled Benchmark Rewriting and Analogical Reasoning for Deceptive Out-of-Distribution Scenarios
summary: Tool-using agent systems powered by large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across web, app, operating-system, and transactional environments. Yet existing safety benchmarks still emphasize explicit risks, potentially overstating a model's ability to judge deceptive or ambiguous trajectories. To address this gap, we introduce ROME (Red-team Orchestrated Multi-agent Evolution), a controlled benchmark-construction pipeline that rewrites known unsafe trajectories into more deceptive evaluation instances while preserving their underlying risk labels. Starting from 100 unsafe source trajectories, ROME produces 300 challenge instances spanning contextual ambiguity, implicit risks, and shortcut decision-making. Experiments show that these challenge sets substantially degrade safety-judgment performance, with hidden-risk cases remaining particularly non-trivial even for recent frontier models. We further study ARISE (Analogical Reasoning for Inference-time Safety Enhancement), a retrieval-guided inference-time enhancement that retrieves ReAct-style analogical safety trajectories from an external analogical base and injects them as structured reasoning exemplars. ARISE improves judgment quality without retraining, but is best viewed as a task-specific robustness enhancement rather than a standalone safety guarantee. Together, ROME and ARISE provide practical tools for stress-testing and improving agent safety judgment under deceptive distribution shifts.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces ROME, a pipeline that transforms known unsafe agent trajectories into more deceptive benchmark instances, and ARISE, a retrieval-guided inference-time enhancement that improves safety judgment via analogical reasoning exemplars. Experiments show ROME-generated challenges degrade judgment performance across frontier models, while ARISE improves robustness without retraining.
AI.motivation: Existing safety benchmarks for LLM-based tool-using agent systems emphasize explicit risks, potentially overstating models' ability to judge deceptive or ambiguous trajectories. There is a gap in evaluating agent safety judgment under more subtle, distribution-shifted scenarios.
AI.method: ROME (Red-team Orchestrated Multi-agent Evolution) rewrites 100 unsafe source trajectories into 300 challenge instances spanning contextual ambiguity, implicit risks, and shortcut decision-making. ARISE (Analogical Reasoning for Inference-time Safety Enhancement) retrieves ReAct-style analogical safety trajectories from an external base and injects them as structured reasoning exemplars during inference.
AI.result: ROME-produced challenge sets substantially degrade safety-judgment performance across models; hidden-risk cases remain particularly difficult even for frontier models. ARISE improves judgment quality without requiring retraining.
AI.conclusion: ROME and ARISE serve as practical tools for stress-testing and improving agent safety judgment under deceptive distribution shifts. ARISE is best viewed as a task-specific robustness enhancement rather than a standalone safety guarantee.

title: RoboAlign-R1: Distilled Multimodal Reward Alignment for Robot Video World Models
summary: Existing robot video world models are typically trained with low-level objectives such as reconstruction and perceptual similarity, which are poorly aligned with the capabilities that matter most for robot decision making, including instruction following, manipulation success, and physical plausibility. They also suffer from error accumulation in long-horizon autoregressive prediction. We present RoboAlign-R1, a framework that combines reward-aligned post-training with stabilized long-horizon inference for robot video world models. We construct RobotWorldBench, a benchmark of 10,000 annotated video-instruction pairs collected from four robot data sources, and train a multimodal teacher judge, RoboAlign-Judge, to provide fine-grained six-dimensional evaluation of generated videos. We then distill the teacher into a lightweight student reward model for efficient reinforcement-learning-based post-training. To reduce long-horizon rollout drift, we further introduce Sliding Window Re-encoding (SWR), a training-free inference strategy that periodically refreshes the generation context. Under our in-domain evaluation protocol, RoboAlign-R1 improves the aggregate six-dimension score by 10.1% over the strongest baseline, including gains of 7.5% on Manipulation Accuracy and 4.6% on Instruction Following; these ranking improvements are further supported by an external VLM-based cross-check and a blinded human study. Meanwhile, SWR improves long-horizon prediction quality with only about 1% additional latency, yielding a 2.8% gain in SSIM and a 9.8% reduction in LPIPS. Together, these results show that reward-aligned post-training and stabilized long-horizon decoding improve task consistency, physical realism, and long-horizon prediction quality in robot video world models.

AI.tldr: RoboAlign-R1 improves robot video world models via reward-aligned post-training (using a distilled reward model from a multimodal judge) and Sliding Window Re-encoding (SWR) for stable long-horizon prediction, achieving significant gains across six evaluation dimensions including manipulation accuracy and instruction following.
AI.motivation: Existing robot video world models are trained with low-level objectives (reconstruction, perceptual similarity) that misalign with robot-relevant capabilities (instruction following, manipulation success, physical plausibility), and suffer from error accumulation in long-horizon autoregressive prediction.
AI.method: Construct RobotWorldBench (10K annotated video-instruction pairs); train RoboAlign-Judge (multimodal teacher for six-dimensional evaluation); distill teacher into lightweight student reward model for RL-based post-training; introduce Sliding Window Re-encoding (SWR) — a training-free inference strategy that periodically refreshes generation context to reduce long-horizon drift.
AI.result: RoboAlign-R1 improves aggregate six-dimension score by 10.1% over strongest baseline (7.5% on Manipulation Accuracy, 4.6% on Instruction Following); SWR yields 2.8% SSIM gain and 9.8% LPIPS reduction with ~1% additional latency; improvements validated by external VLM cross-check and blinded human study.
AI.conclusion: Reward-aligned post-training and stabilized long-horizon decoding (SWR) improve task consistency, physical realism, and long-horizon prediction quality in robot video world models.

title: Revisiting the Travel Planning Capabilities of Large Language Models
summary: Travel planning serves as a critical task for long-horizon reasoning, exposing significant deficits in LLMs. However, existing benchmarks and evaluations primarily assess final plans in an end-to-end manner, which lacks interpretability and makes it difficult to analyze the root causes of failures. To bridge this gap, we decompose travel planning into five constituent atomic sub-capabilities, including \emph{Constraint Extraction}, \emph{Tool Use}, \emph{Plan Generation}, \emph{Error Identification}, and \emph{Error Correction}. We implement a decoupled evaluation protocol leveraging oracle intermediate contexts to rigorously isolate these components, thereby measuring the atomic performance boundary without the noise of cascading errors. Our results highlight a clear contrast in performance: while LLMs are proficient in extracting explicit constraints, they struggle to infer implicit, open-world requirements. Furthermore, they exhibit structural biases in plan generation and suffer from ineffective self-correction, characterized by excessive sensitivity and erroneous persistence.
